parking.disabled_body: Once on, every time you switch the car off, it writes an entry. It shows where the car stands, gives you photos from all four cameras after you walk away, lists cars that came or left next to you while the Guardian was awake, and sums it up with “Back at the car” when you return. While it is off, nothing runs.
parking.no_sessions: The first entry appears when you next switch the car off.
parking.gps_stale: Position is old — in a garage?
parking.sentry_lock_wait: Waiting for the car to lock
parking.sentry_vehicle_on_only: Only while the car is on
parking.signage_pending: Not read yet. A Guardian clip was being recorded, so this waits. It tries again soon, and at the latest when your next drive begins.
parking.signage_unavailable: Reading signs needs the extra text-reading files (models/signage_*.tflite).
parking.signage_skipped: There were no pictures to read.
parking.signage_none: No text found for floor, zone or space.
parking.no_neighbours: No cars nearby were noted. The Guardian has to be awake for that.
parking.no_events: The Guardian recorded nothing during this stop.
parking.delete_confirm: Delete this entry with its photos and pictures?
parking.delete_failed: Could not delete. Is the car still parked here?
parking.requeue_failed: Not running. Turn on the parking log first.
parking.settings_desc: Writes an entry every time you switch the car off: where it stands, how recent the GPS position is, photos from all four cameras when you walk away and when you return, and cars that came or left next to you while the Guardian was awake. You also get two alerts, “Parked” and “Back at the car”. When off, nothing runs and nothing is stored.
parking.settings_snapshots: Photos when you leave and return
parking.settings_snapshots_desc: Photos from all four cameras about 90 seconds after switch-off, and again at the first door opening or unlocking. They also appear in the alerts.
parking.settings_neighbours_desc: Notes which cars arrive or leave next to you, based on what the Guardian saw, and keeps the clearest pictures of each. The Guardian must be awake.
parking.settings_signage_desc: Reads the floor, zone or space number from the photos and the last minute of the drive-in video. Text reading (PP-OCRv3, about 5.5 MB) runs on the car itself. It runs once right after the first photos, so the “Parked” alert can name the floor. If a Guardian clip is being recorded, it waits and tries again later. Files for other languages can be copied to Panoptes/models/.
parking.settings_geocoding_desc: Turns the parking position into a street or district name for the “Parked” alert and your list. Until you choose here, the parking log uses the place-naming choice of your Guardian or drive camera.
parking.settings_geocoding_online_desc: If the car cannot name the place by itself, it asks OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Only the parking coordinates and the language of the device are sent.
parking.settings_geocoding_inherited: Using the choice from your Guardian or drive camera. Switch something here to decide for the parking log alone.
parking.settings_end_trigger_desc: When a parking entry is closed. "When I return": at the first door opening or unlocking (or when the car powers on). "When the car powers on": opening a door or unlocking only refreshes the new pictures. "When I drive away": waits until the car leaves P. If the gear can't be read, the entry closes about 2 minutes after power-on.

road_sense.bs_enable_desc: When you switch on the indicator, a small floating window shows the rear and side cameras as one picture. You set its size and place below. Left indicator: back and left. Right indicator: right and back.
road_sense.bs_merge_desc: Show the rear and side cameras as one picture, or just one camera. A single camera fills the window with its whole view. The sliders “Blend point” and “Soft blend edge” only work for the combined picture.
road_sense.bs_rotation_desc: Turns the picture of a single camera. Handy when a side camera is easier to read upright. The window changes shape to fit.
road_sense.bs_rotation_left_desc: Turns the picture of the left camera, shown for a left turn. 40° and 310° are ready-made blind-spot views. They also set their own crop, mirroring and zoom, so you need to change nothing else. The window changes shape to fit.
road_sense.bs_rotation_right_desc: Turns the picture of the right camera, shown for a right turn. It is a mirror image of the left one, so it often needs another angle. 40° and 310° are ready-made blind-spot views. They also set their own crop, mirroring and zoom, so you need to change nothing else. The window changes shape to fit.
road_sense.bs_auto_base_desc: The angle used when you drive forward. In reverse the picture turns by 180°, so it still reads the right way up.
road_sense.bs_rectify_desc: Flattens the barrel-shaped bend of the wide-angle lens in single-camera views of the side and back. Higher values flatten more but cut off a bit of the edge. Does not apply to the combined picture.
road_sense.bs_display_desc: Where the blind-spot picture appears. “Driver display” puts it in the dial area behind the steering wheel. While an indicator is on, it replaces the dials for a moment and they come back when you stop indicating.
road_sense.bs_cluster_layout_desc: Pick the size of your driver display. If the picture looks stretched or cut off, try another one.
road_sense.bs_calib_desc: Tap a side to open a live preview on the car screen, then move the sliders below to line it up. The preview floats over this page. If it covers the controls, tap “Hide preview”, or move it with the place settings above and press “Apply”. Apply once it looks right.
road_sense.bs_needs_overlay: To show the blind-spot view, allow “Display over other apps”
road_sense.master_enable_desc: Spots bumps, potholes and speed humps using the car’s movement and GPS, and warns you before known ones. All other road watch settings only count while this is on.
road_sense.map_open_desc: Opens the full-screen map. Search for routes, navigate and see danger spots on the way. Tap a spot to confirm or remove it.
road_sense.map_open_hint: Start the map from the app in the car.
road_sense.routing_help: The map itself is free. Turn-by-turn directions need a free personal key from a Valhalla provider. Paste yours here. It is optional: the map and danger spots work without it. The key is stored in encrypted form on the car.
road_sense.routing_guide_title: How to get a free key
road_sense.routing_step1: Tap “Free key from Stadia Maps”. The Stadia Maps sign-up opens. Make a free account (the free plan needs no credit card).
road_sense.routing_step2: In the dashboard, open Properties and create a Property. Then go to Authentication and API Keys.
road_sense.routing_step3: Click “Create API key” and copy the key you see.
road_sense.routing_step4: Paste it into the field “Key for route calculation” below and tap Save. Keep the web address as it is.
road_sense.routing_endpoint_desc: The address of the Valhalla-compatible service. Leave it as is unless your provider gives you another.
road_sense.routing_key_desc: Your own key. It is stored encrypted on the car and not shown again after saving.
road_sense.routing_key_set_ph: A key is saved. Paste a new one to replace it.
road_sense.map_cluster_project: Show the map on the driver display
road_sense.map_cluster_project_desc: Shows the whole map in the dial area behind the steering wheel and takes the place of the dials while it runs. The blind-spot camera still pops up on top when you indicate.
road_sense.map_cluster_auto_desc: Puts the map on the driver display by itself every time the car is switched on.
road_sense.map_cluster_auto_conflict_title: Another app is using the driver display
road_sense.map_cluster_auto_conflict_body: The screen-casting page is set to send an app to the driver display at start. The display can only show one thing at a time. Switch that off and show the map instead?
road_sense.map_cluster_layout_desc: Pick the size of your driver display. It is the same setting as for the blind-spot view. If the map looks stretched or cut off, try another one.
road_sense.calibration_enable: Check each find on the screen
road_sense.calibration_enable_desc: Shows every spot found on screen with buttons to confirm or correct it, so you can teach road watch which finds are real. Use it for a few drives to tune it to your car, then switch it off.
road_sense.overlay_show_desc: Shows the small floating road watch badge and the card for a danger spot. Switch it off to hide them. Spotting, warning sounds and sharing carry on in the background. Only the display goes away.
road_sense.detect_sensitivity_desc: How quickly a bump, pothole or speed hump counts as a find. 50 % is the standard. Move toward “More” to catch milder spots (and a few false alarms). Move toward “Less” to only count clear, hard jolts. This changes what gets found. It is not the same as “Minimum certainty” for warnings below.
road_sense.warn_enable_desc: Warns you as you get close to a spot that is already known on your route.
road_sense.warn_mode_desc: How you are told when a danger spot is ahead.
road_sense.warn_channel_desc: Which audio channel plays the warning tone. “Navigation” uses the car’s guidance channel. The tone then turns your music down instead of fighting it, and follows the navigation volume.
road_sense.warn_test_desc: Plays the loudest warning tone now on the channel above, so you can check the top volume you set. The real warning only sounds when you drive toward a known danger spot.
road_sense.warn_test_playing: Tone sent at the volume you chose
road_sense.warn_lead_desc: How many seconds before the danger spot the warning comes. Higher gives you more time to react. Lower warns closer to the spot.
road_sense.warn_conf_desc: Only warn about spots the app is at least this sure of. 0 warns about every known spot. Higher values skip the doubtful ones.
road_sense.warn_severity_desc: Choose which kinds of spots trigger a warning. Switch off the small ones if you only want to hear about the worst.
road_sense.crowd_note: Normally everything stays on this device. Sending and receiving are separate. Turning one on does not turn on the other.
road_sense.crowd_upload_desc: Sends your finds without your name to the shared map, to make it better. Off at first: until you switch this on, everything stays on the device.
road_sense.crowd_download_desc: Fetches spots that other drivers reported, so you get warned about places you haven’t driven over yet. Off at first.
road_sense.crowd_worker_url_desc: Optional. Send and fetch via your own sync server instead of the standard one.
road_sense.delete_local_desc: Removes the finds and settings kept on this device. This can’t be undone.
road_sense.delete_cloud_title: Delete data from the shared map
road_sense.delete_cloud_desc: Removes the finds you shared from the shared map. Data from other drivers stays. This can’t be undone.
road_sense.confirm_delete_local: Delete everything road watch has saved on this device? This can’t be undone.
road_sense.confirm_delete_cloud: Remove the finds you shared from the shared map? This can’t be undone.
road_sense.bs_reverse_desc: Hides the blind-spot view in reverse gear, so it doesn’t cover the reversing camera.
road_sense.bs_speed_range_desc: Shows the blind-spot view only within this speed range. Leave both at 0 (any) to show it at every speed. Handy to keep it away in slow traffic or on the motorway.
road_sense.warn_volume_desc: Sets the top volume of road watch warnings. Small and medium spots always sound softer than serious ones.
road_sense.bs_speed_any: Any speed. It always shows when you indicate.
road_sense.bs_speed_err_order: The top speed can’t be lower than the bottom speed.
road_sense.bs_speed_err_range: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max} km/h (0 = any).
road_sense.bs_speed_max_aria: Top speed in km/h, 0 for any
road_sense.bs_speed_min_aria: Bottom speed in km/h, 0 for any
road_sense.bs_speed_not_loaded: The saved speed range couldn’t be read. Reload the page before you change it.

Open this page on your phone through your HTTPS address and add it to the home screen. Then come back here and turn notifications on.
notif.backend_banner: Notifications are not set up on this car yet. The car needs a fixed HTTPS address for this (your own reverse proxy).
notif.push_delivery_sub: Turns on alerts for the device you're using right now. Do this once on every phone where you install the page.
notif.categories_sub: Choose which alerts this device gets. A topic sends an alert when the car's screen notices the matching event. What sets it off depends on the settings of the related service.
notif.devices_sub: Every phone with alerts turned on is listed here. Remove takes a device off the list on the car's side. Turn off here (above) also stops alerts in this browser.
notif.perm_zrok_required: Phone notifications need a fixed HTTPS address. See the note above.
notif.perm_unsupported_install: Alerts don't work here. On Safari, add the page to your home screen first.
notif.perm_granted: Alerts are on for this device
notif.perm_denied: Alerts are blocked. Allow them in your browser settings.
notif.enable_first: Turn on alerts for this device first.
notif.remove_device_confirm: Stop sending alerts to this device?
notif.remove_device_tombstoned: Removed. For 30 minutes, alerts can't be turned on again from this device. Changed your mind? Turn them on again from this page after that.
notif.pwa_not_loaded: The app part isn't loaded. Put the page on your home screen first.
notif.enable_success: Alerts are now on for this device.
notif.disabled_on_device: Alerts are off for this device.
notif.backend_not_initialized: Notifications are not set up on this car yet.
notif.test_sent: Test sent. Look for it in your phone's alerts.
notif.subscribe_browser_error: Your browser said no to phone alerts: {error}. Try another browser. These are known to fail here: Samsung Internet without Google Play Services, Brave with Shields on, and Edge when it has outages.
notif.tunnel_unreachable: The car cannot be reached. The HTTPS address no longer answers. Check that remote access is running and reload the page.
notif.sev_critical: Critical: urgent alert. The banner stays on screen, the phone buzzes longer, and quiet hours don't apply.
notif.sev_warn: Warning: short buzz and a normal banner. Worth a look soon.
notif.sev_auto: Auto: the car picks the level for each event from its data. A slow leak gives a warning, a fast leak is critical.
notif.sev_info: Info: quiet banner, no buzz. Only for confirmations.
notif.min_importance_sub: One limit for this whole device, on top of the topics above. Raise it to mute minor alerts in one go. "Warning and up" skips all notes and info (everyday Guardian events, charging started or stopped) but still lets alerts and critical ones through. Skipped alerts still show up in the log.
notif.telegram_sub: Sends Guardian events to a Telegram chat you've linked. Link the bot in the Telegram settings. The switches below decide which levels reach the chat. Muted levels are still logged. Only the message is skipped.
notif.telegram_delivery_sub: Which kinds of events go to Telegram. This is separate from the level filter above. Each switch turns a whole topic on or off.
notif.vehicle_layout_sub: Choose the side of the car where the driver sits. This tells door alerts whether the front doors are called Front left or Front right. It's saved right away and counts from the next door event. No restart needed.
notif.drive_lhd_sub: The driver sits on the left. That's most of Europe, North America and China.
notif.drive_rhd_sub: The driver sits on the right. That's the UK, Australia, India and Japan.
notif.tyre_limits_sub: Set the normal pressure for each axle. A tyre under the lowest or over the highest value triggers a warning. Under the critical value you get a flat-tyre alert. These values drive phone and Telegram alerts and the corner colours under Controls. The defaults suit standard tyres. Change them if the sticker in your car says otherwise.
notif.tyre_axle_note: Normal range: lowest and highest value.
notif.tyre_critical_note: At or under this value, the alert becomes critical. It counts for all four tyres and can't be higher than the lowest value of either axle.
notif.tyre_reset_hint: Standard values are back. Tap Save to keep them.
notif.tyre_load_failed: Couldn't load your saved values. Showing the standard ones.
notif.tyre_err_range: Use a whole number from {min} to {max} kPa.
notif.tyre_err_order: The highest value must be above the lowest.
notif.tyre_err_critical: The critical value can't be above the lowest value of either axle.
notif.tyre_unit_note: The unit used for tyre pressure on the pages and in alerts. The limits below are always entered in kPa.

surveillance_motion.label: Motion detected (old)
surveillance_motion.note: Old combined category, kept only for compatibility. Better use the three levels Notice, Alert and Critical below.

surveillance_motion_notice.label: Guardian – Notice
surveillance_motion_notice.note: Normal movement or someone walking past. Off by default – turn it on if you want to hear about every event.

surveillance_motion_alert.label: Guardian – Alert
surveillance_motion_alert.note: A person is close to the car, a vehicle is approaching, or something is happening right at the car.

surveillance_motion_critical.label: Guardian – Critical
surveillance_motion_critical.note: A person is very close or stays at the car. Check right away.

surveillance_proximity.label: Proximity
surveillance_proximity.note: Distance and trigger depend on the recording settings.

surveillance_ai_off.label: AI detection off
surveillance_ai_off.note: The AI model is not running; until it is back, the Guardian records on any motion.

surveillance_guard_stop.label: Guardian paused / back on
surveillance_guard_stop.note: The Guardian pauses to save the battery (low charge, weak 12 V battery, parked too long, quiet times or quiet zones).

vehicle_health_tyre_pressure.label: Tyre pressure warning
vehicle_health_tyre_pressure.note: The tyre pressure sensor reports too little or too much pressure.

vehicle_health_tyre_leak.label: Tyre losing air
vehicle_health_tyre_leak.note: The tyre pressure sensor reports a slow or fast loss of pressure.

vehicle_security_door_opened.label: Door opened
vehicle_security_door_opened.note: When a door, the bonnet or the boot is opened while the car is parked (switched off).

vehicle_security_door_closed.label: Door closed
vehicle_security_door_closed.note: When a door, the bonnet or the boot is closed while the car is parked (switched off).

vehicle_charging_started.label: Charging started
vehicle_charging_started.note: When the battery management reports that charging has begun.

vehicle_charging_stopped.label: Charging stopped
vehicle_charging_stopped.note: With a 10 s delay so short gaps while plugging in or at a fast charger do not count.

vehicle_charging_full.label: Charging complete
vehicle_charging_full.note: Once per charge, when the battery is nearly full or the battery management reports charging as finished. Not when you plug in a car that is already full. Also comes during quiet hours so you remember to unplug.

vehicle_charging_fault.label: Charging fault
vehicle_charging_fault.note: The battery management reports a fault at the AC or DC charger, the charging plug or the on-board charger.

vehicle_health_soh_frame_mismatch.label: Battery capacity does not match
vehicle_health_soh_frame_mismatch.note: Once, when the capacity reported by the battery management differs by more than 15% from the one entered – usually nominal instead of usable capacity on a plug-in hybrid. The battery dialog fixes it with one tap.

automation_action.label: Rule triggered
automation_action.note: Comes when a rule contains the action “Send notification”.

genai_insight.label: AI note ready
genai_insight.note: Only when notifications for AI notes are explicitly turned on.

parking_session_started.label: Parked – where and what is around
parking_session_started.note: About 90 s after switching off: place, how fresh the GPS is, whether the Guardian is on, and a still from all four cameras. Needs the parking analysis in the Guardian settings.

parking_session_ended.label: Back at the car – what happened
parking_session_ended.note: At the first unlock or door opening: how long you were away, how many Guardian events there were and how many vehicles came or left next to you.

network_hotspot_limit.label: Hotspot data limit reached
network_hotspot_limit.note: When the hotspot goes over its set data limit; it is turned off at the same time. Raise or reset the limit to use it again.

notif.telegram_kat_hier: Which messages reach your Telegram chat is set on the Telegram page – each category separately.
notif.telegram_sub2: Sends messages to a connected Telegram chat. Connect the bot and choose the categories on the Telegram page.

charge.title: Charging
charge.subtitle: See how your car charges and how much power it uses
charge.quality_warning_short: Values that don't add up are hidden.
charge.quality_info_open: Why are some charging values hidden?
charge.quality_info_body:
Panoptes found a charge on normal AC power with a top power of 25 kW or more. That can't be right for this plug type, and it matches an old fault in the car's data. The charge itself, its readings, its cost and your totals are not changed. Panoptes only hides the energy, average power and top power of that one charge, so wrong numbers don't pass as real.

The LFP check badge is a separate thing. It needs a full run from 10% battery or lower up to 99% or higher, and an LFP battery in the car model you set up. It does not make the hidden power values correct.
charge.power_waiting: Shows after your first recorded charge
charge.estimated_explanation: When the car doesn't report a value directly, Panoptes marks it as estimated. Estimated power is worked out from the battery data. Estimated energy and cost come from how the battery changed and from your price. The top power only comes from real readings.
charge.chart_energy_sub: kWh added in each charge. DC is blue, AC is teal.
charge.summary_range_desc: Range gained by charging (estimated from the energy charged)
charge.stats_intro: What your charging looks like over time
charge.range_pick: Choose a first or last day
charge.range_order: The first day must come before the last day
charge.delete_confirm: Delete this charge? You can't get it back.
charge.edit_cost_prompt: Type the total cost of this charge. Leave it empty to start over.
charge.cannot_edit_in_progress_cost: The cost can't be changed while the car is still charging
charge.invalid_cost: Type a number that is zero or more
charge.no_location: No place saved for this charge
charge.detail_no_samples: No curve was saved for this charge
charge.settings_auto_record_desc: Keeps a record of each charge with power, cost and battery values
charge.settings_rate_desc: Price per kWh. The Logbook uses the same one.
charge.settings_dc_rate_desc: Own price for fast DC charging. Leave at 0 to use the normal price.
charge.settings_clear_desc: Removes all saved charges and curves for good
charge.settings_clear_confirm: Delete the whole charging history? You can't get it back.
charge.baking_note: More details show up with every new charge you finish
charge.no_data_hint: Trends and totals show up after your first saved charge
charge.disabled_hint: Turn on charging records in Settings to begin
charge.no_sessions_hint: Charges are added by themselves once you plug in
charge.tariffs_desc: Save a price for a place. Charges there use it by themselves. The prices above count everywhere else.
charge.tariffs_empty_hint: Add one for the place where you usually charge. Every charge there is priced for you.
charge.tariff_add_here: Add a price for this place
charge.tariff_dc_rate_hint: Leave empty if DC costs the same here
charge.tariff_radius_hint: How near a charge has to be to use this price
charge.tariff_limit: That's the most prices you can have

tariff_repriced.one: {count} earlier charge got a new price
tariff_repriced.other: {count} earlier charges got a new price

charge.tariff_confirm_delete: Delete this price? Charges that used it switch to your other prices.
charge.tariff_err_no_rate: Type in an AC or DC price
charge.tariff_err_no_gps: No GPS yet. A price needs a place to go with.

scores.consistency_text: Shows how even your driving is over the whole drive. Switching between rough and calm lowers this score.
scores.consistency_tip: 💡 Tip: Choose one way of driving and stay with it. Steady habits become second nature and save power.

automation.variables_help_intro: A variable is a name with a value that the app keeps in mind. One rule sets it, another reads it. You pick the name yourself (e.g. Parking_Mode) and type it exactly the same everywhere, capitals included. The value is free text: true or false, or a word like sport.
automation.variables_help_unset: A variable you never set counts as empty. So “not equal to true” is already true until you set it.
automation.variables_help_mutex: So a routine can't start again while it is running: add the condition Parking_Mode ≠ true. Make the first action Set Parking_Mode = true. In the rule that ends the routine, set it back to false.
automation.operating_mode_help_intro: This covers all of Panoptes's background services, not only the guardian.
automation.operating_mode_help_on_only: On only: once ACC goes off, rules that are due still finish. Then every Panoptes service stops until ACC is on again.
automation.operating_mode_help_on_and_off: On + off: Panoptes keeps running after ACC goes off. That way the guardian and the background checks carry on while parked. It takes more power from the battery.

automation.run_shell_description: Runs a shell command in the background service whenever this rule starts. It works on its own, so it needs the extra shell permission for rules (off unless you turn it on).
automation.allow_shell_desc: Lets rules run raw shell commands by themselves once their conditions are met. This happens in the background with nobody watching. Keep it off unless you know exactly what your rules do.

automation.safety_warning: These locks apply to car actions started from Panoptes's Rules, action groups, Buttons, Shortcuts, MQTT, Controls and saved seat positions. automation.safety_unavailable: Can't show the safety locks. Their current state couldn't be checked. Reload the page and try again.
automation.safety_disable_confirm: Turn this lock off? The action will then work while the car is moving or its state is unknown.
automation.safety_door_locks_desc: Doors can only be locked or unlocked while the car is safely parked.
automation.safety_trunk_desc: Opening or closing the tailgate is blocked. Stop still works.
automation.safety_mirror_fold_desc: Folding in the outside mirrors is blocked. Folding them out still works.
automation.safety_positioning: Moving seats, steering wheel and mirrors
automation.safety_positioning_desc: Recalling seat memory and moving to saved positions is blocked. The car itself may also ask for Park.
automation.safety_headlight_off_desc: Choosing “Off” for the headlights is blocked. Auto, parking lights and low beam still work.
automation.safety_display_brightness_desc: Changing the brightness of the main screen, the driver display and the head-up display is blocked.
automation.safety_display_power_desc: Switching screens on or off and switching the head-up display off is blocked. Switching the head-up display on still works.
automation.safety_screen_media_desc: Playback on the full screen is blocked. Sound through the speakers still works.
automation.shell_warning: Runs on its own in the background each time this rule starts. A wrong command can upset the car's screen unit. Needs the shell permission for rules.

recording.clip_duration_warning: Longer clips mean fewer, bigger files. But a clip is only saved once it ends. surveillance.confirm_disable_all_classes: Smart object recognition goes off completely. The Guardian then reacts to any movement and starts at most one new clip every 30 seconds. You may miss real events.
surveillance.enable_desc: Watches the cameras for movement and objects
surveillance.accoff_mode_desc: Events only films when something happens. Non-stop films the whole time the car is parked, with no filters and no smart recognition.
surveillance.accoff_hint_smart: Movement plus smart recognition. Filming starts only when something moves and the camera spots a person, a vehicle or another relevant object.
surveillance.accoff_hint_continuous: Plain non-stop filming. All four cameras run for as long as the Guardian is awake, with no movement filter and no smart recognition. Needs much more storage.
surveillance.arm_mode_desc: When the Guardian wakes up after the car is switched off. Both options respect quiet zones and schedules.
surveillance.arm_hint_lock: Wakes up when you lock the doors and goes back to sleep when you unlock, so it doesn't film you. If your car can't report the lock state, it wakes up 60 seconds after switch-off instead.
surveillance.arm_hint_power: Wakes up the moment the car is switched off and sleeps again when it is switched on. Works in every car, but may film you as you walk away.
surveillance.arm_saved_lock: Wakes up when you lock the doors
surveillance.arm_saved_power: Wakes up when the car is switched off
surveillance.operating_mode_desc: Whether Panoptes keeps running once the car is off. With „Driving only“ Panoptes shuts down fully when you park. Features while you drive (drive camera, logbook, charging) are not affected.
surveillance.operating_mode_hint_on_off: Panoptes keeps an eye on things while parked: the Guardian and the background checks stay active. Uses a little battery overnight.
surveillance.operating_mode_hint_on_only: Panoptes switches off completely when you turn the car off: nothing runs in the background, the Guardian sleeps and no battery is used. Drive camera, logbook and charging still work while you drive, and everything starts again by itself the next time you switch the car on.
surveillance.operating_mode_saved_on_only: Switches off together with the car
surveillance.operating_mode_postoff_disabled_note: These settings apply after the car is off. With „Driving only“ Panoptes shuts down when you park, so they do nothing. Switch to „Always on“ to use them.
surveillance.keep_usb_power_desc: Keeps the USB ports powered after the car is off, for example to charge a phone or run an accessory. Turn it off so the screen unit can sleep and the starter battery (12 V) is spared. Note: the SD card slot shares the same power, so the card goes off too while parked and the Guardian saves to the built-in storage instead. Applies from the next time you switch the car off.
surveillance.mobile_data_keepalive: Keep mobile data on when parked
surveillance.mobile_data_keepalive_desc: On some models the mobile data module falls asleep a while after the car is off, and the car drops off the network. Turn this on to keep it awake. Better leave it off unless you really lose the connection while parked, because staying connected costs extra battery and data. Works only if mobile data was already on when you parked. Applies from the next time you switch the car off.
surveillance.mobile_data_keepalive_saved_on: Mobile data stays on when parked (from the next switch-off)
surveillance.mobile_data_keepalive_saved_off: Mobile data is left as it is when parked
surveillance.mobile_data_keepalive_save_failed: Couldn't save the mobile data setting
surveillance.di5_cloud_keepalive: Experiment: keep DiLink 5 awake through the BYD account
surveillance.di5_cloud_keepalive_desc: While the car is off, asks for the car status through your BYD account every 15 seconds. Needs a connected BYD account and internet. May use data from the car's SIM, stop deep sleep and drain more battery while parked. Stops when the car is switched on or when the background service stops.
surveillance.di5_cloud_keepalive_requires_cloud: Connect your BYD account and check it first, then you can turn this on.
surveillance.di5_cloud_keepalive_saved_on: Keeping DiLink 5 awake via the BYD account: on
surveillance.di5_cloud_keepalive_saved_off: Keeping DiLink 5 awake via the BYD account: off
surveillance.di5_qnx_keepalive: Experiment: keep DiLink 5 awake through the car's own network (QNX)
surveillance.di5_qnx_keepalive_desc: While the car is off, the QNX system of the screen unit is asked every 30 seconds to keep the car's network awake (the same request the firmware sends during over-the-air updates). No cloud and no internet needed. Uses more of the starter battery (12 V): it stops after the time limit below, or when the 12 V reading falls under 12 V.
surveillance.di5_qnx_keepalive_minutes: Stay awake for no longer than (minutes)
surveillance.di5_qnx_keepalive_saved: Saved. Applies at the next check while parked.
surveillance.di5_parked_keepalive: Experiment: keep DiLink 5 awake while parked
surveillance.di5_parked_keepalive_desc: For DiLink 5 screen units, with any camera mode. Holds the car in Guardian mode after it is switched off, so the control unit (MCU) doesn't cut the power to the cameras and USB, and wakes it again if it dozes off. Uses more of the starter battery (12 V). It stops by itself below the voltage limit you set and stays off until the car is switched on or charging is detected. Applies at the next check while parked.
surveillance.di5_parked_keepalive_confirm_body: This is an experiment. While the car is off, it holds the car in Guardian mode and wakes the control unit (MCU) again and again, which uses more of the starter battery (12 V). It stops by itself below the voltage limit and stays off until the car is switched on or charging is detected. Every write to the hardware is logged, so you can check it on your own car.
surveillance.di5_parked_keepalive_confirm_unavailable: No confirmation possible, so this stays off
surveillance.di5_parked_keepalive_saved_on: Keeping DiLink 5 awake while parked: on (applies at the next check)
surveillance.di5_parked_keepalive_saved_off: Keeping DiLink 5 awake while parked: off
surveillance.low_power_mode_desc: Saves battery while parked: when nothing is going on, the camera runs at a low frame rate (about 5 fps), and jumps back to full quality the moment movement is detected. Detection works as usual, so the same events are caught, but footage from quiet moments looks choppier. Applies while the car is parked and the Guardian is awake.
surveillance.low_power_saved_on: Power-saving mode on: the camera idles at a low frame rate while parked
surveillance.low_power_saved_off: Power-saving mode off: the camera keeps its full frame rate while parked
surveillance.low_soc_cutoff_desc: When the battery falls to this level, the Guardian stops and the car goes to sleep, so the battery isn't drained empty. Set to Off if it should never stop because of a low battery.
surveillance.low_soc_cutoff_hint: A higher value spares the battery more, but the Guardian stops sooner. With Off it keeps watching until the battery is almost empty.
surveillance.keep_usb_saved_off: USB goes to sleep when parked (from the next switch-off)
surveillance.usb_off_storage_notice: USB power is off, so the SD card has no power while parked. The Guardian saves to the built-in storage until USB is switched on again.
surveillance.usb_off_confirm_body: The SD card runs on the same power as USB, so it has no power while parked. The Guardian will switch to the built-in storage so filming keeps working. Once USB is on again, you can switch back to the SD card.
surveillance.usb_off_confirm_unavailable: No confirmation possible, so USB power stays on
surveillance.usb_off_switched_internal: USB power is off — the Guardian now saves to the built-in storage
surveillance.storage_blocked_usb_off: Turn on „Keep USB on when parked“ to use SD or USB while parked
surveillance.safe_desc: No filming when you park here
surveillance.env_desc: A quick setup for your usual spot
surveillance.det_zone_desc: How far from the car movement must be to count
surveillance.custom_config: Your own setup — pick a preset to go back to the recommended values.

distance.1_hint: Near — only large or close things (cars, groups)
distance.2_hint: Fairly near — good for car parks, notices people close by
distance.3_hint: Balanced — notices people up to about 8 m away
distance.4_hint: Far — picks up distant movement, may include people walking past
distance.5_hint: Very far — longest reach, best for quiet places

sens.1_hint: Strict — only big things (car, group); lone passers-by are ignored
sens.2_hint: Careful — solid objects only, good for windy days
sens.3_hint: Balanced — reacts to people walking, ignores insects and leaves
sens.4_hint: Keen — reacts the moment something moves into view
sens.5_hint: Very keen — reacts to every movement, only for garages and indoors

v2_sens_hint.1: Reacts only to big, close movement, like someone touching the car.
v2_sens_hint.2: Notices solid things nearby. Good on windy days.
v2_sens_hint.3: Balanced — notices a person coming closer than about 3 meters.
v2_sens_hint.4: Keen — reacts quickly, good for people further away.
v2_sens_hint.5: Highest — reacts to any movement in the picture. More false alarms are possible.

env_hint.outdoor: Standard setup for open car parks and driveways. Copes with sun, clouds and headlights.
env_hint.garage: Strong light filtering for indoor parking. Ignores flickering tube lights and reflections.
env_hint.street: Made for busy places with people on foot. Waits a bit longer so passers-by are ignored.

zone_hint.close: Counts only what happens close to the car: roughly the lower third of each camera picture (about 3 m on the rear camera). Cuts out most false alarms from passing traffic.
zone_hint.normal: The usual area: roughly the lower two thirds of each camera picture (about 6 m on the rear camera). The right choice for everyday parking.
zone_hint.extended: No distance limit — the whole camera picture counts, even across the street. Expect more triggers from passing traffic.

shadow_hint.0: Shadow filter off. Tree shadows and moving clouds can start clips by mistake.
shadow_hint.1: Light — removes obvious shadows. Good in garages with tube lights.
shadow_hint.2: Balanced — removes most tree shadows and still notices real movement.
shadow_hint.3: Strong — rejects shadows as far as possible. Use it when parked under trees in strong wind.

surveillance.settings_applied_deleting: Settings are active. Deleting about {files} old clips ({size})
surveillance.byd_pwd_keep: Leave empty to keep the current password
surveillance.byd_pin_keep: Leave empty to keep the current PIN
surveillance.byd_pwd_hint: The password you use to log in to the BYD app
surveillance.byd_pin_hint: The PIN with 4 to 6 digits you chose in the official BYD app
surveillance.byd_pwd_pin_required: For the first setup you need the password and the control PIN
surveillance.byd_save_progress: Saving your login and trying it out…
surveillance.byd_request_long: This takes a while… we look again in a moment
surveillance.byd_test_progress: Logging in and flashing the lights…
surveillance.byd_test_sent: ✓ Sent to the car — look at your lights!
surveillance.byd_test_check_car: It may have been sent — look at your car
surveillance.loitering_time_desc: How long someone has to stay near the car before filming starts
surveillance.loitering_time_hint: A longer time ignores people who just walk by. A shorter time reacts faster.
surveillance.approach_trigger_desc: Starts filming earlier once the camera is sure that a real person or vehicle is coming closer, without waiting out the whole waiting time
surveillance.approach_trigger_hint: Choose Off to always wait the full time. A smaller value starts sooner when someone walks up (only when the camera really sees a person or vehicle).
surveillance.shadow_filter_desc: Ignores shadows of trees and clouds and other changes in light that would start clips by mistake
surveillance.motion_salience_desc: Starts on big, close, moving things, even if the camera can't tell what they are
surveillance.motion_salience_hint: Catches what smart recognition misses: someone walking right up to the car in poor light, or a big vehicle pulling in close, where the camera can't name the object. It only starts when the movement is big, close and crosses the picture steadily for about a second, so branches in the wind, shadows, rain and sweeping headlights are still ignored. Expect a few extra clips with no person or vehicle named. They are kept even when „Drop clips without a known object“ is on, because a clip the camera couldn't sort is the last one worth deleting by itself.
surveillance.discard_empty_motion: Drop clips without a known object
surveillance.discard_empty_motion_desc: Strictly throws away clips where no real person or vehicle was followed
surveillance.discard_empty_motion_hint: Useful if shadows or swaying branches give you false alarms: such clips are deleted by themselves when nothing real was followed. Careful: in poor light or unclear scenes, it can now and then throw away a real threat the camera didn't recognise. Keep it off if you would rather keep every clip.
surveillance.discard_empty_motion_night_desc: Uses the shape of the movement instead of the brightness, so dark scenes are covered too
surveillance.discard_empty_motion_night_hint: Normally this filter works in daylight only, because in the dark the camera can miss a real person completely. With this on, night clips are dropped only if the movement looks like leaves in the wind or a change of light (headlights, reflections) and never moves across the picture like a person would. The chance of throwing away a real night event is higher than with the daytime filter, so keep it off if in doubt.
surveillance.camera_controls_desc: Turn watching on or off for each camera
surveillance.camera_controls_hint: Turn off cameras that look at a wall or a busy road to get fewer false alarms.
surveillance.sidecam_boost_desc: Own alertness and watch area for the left and right cameras only. Handy when neighbours park right next to you and the front and rear settings are too relaxed to notice them.
surveillance.detect_objects_desc: The camera works out what caused the movement
surveillance.detect_objects_hint: Choose which things the YOLO recognition should look for. Movement starts a clip either way; recognition only says what was seen.
surveillance.telegram_two_stage_desc: First a short „filming has started“ message, then the photo when it is over. Off normally, because the photo alone is usually enough.
surveillance.telegram_tiers_desc: Choose which levels reach your Telegram chat. Levels that are off are still filmed; only the message is left out.
surveillance.tier_notice_desc: Everyday things (parked cars, movement far away)
surveillance.tier_alert_desc: Someone coming closer, or a vehicle near enough to deserve a look
surveillance.tier_critical_desc: Someone very close to the car — maybe tampering or hanging around
surveillance.motion_heatmap_desc: Shows the watched areas over the picture
surveillance.motion_heatmap_title: Puts coloured squares on the live picture to show where movement is noticed.
surveillance.filter_debug_log_desc: Writes down each filter decision in detail
surveillance.filter_debug_log_title: Writes the details of each filter decision for every detection into the log.
surveillance.detection_zones_hint: Restrict watching to certain parts of each camera picture. When this is off, the whole picture is watched.
surveillance.roi_enable_desc: Draw the area to watch for this camera
surveillance.schedule_enable_desc: The Guardian is awake only on the days and hours you pick
surveillance.schedule_hint: Add the times when the Guardian should be awake. Outside these times it stays asleep, even when the car is off.
surveillance.deterrent_on_motion_desc: What the car does through your BYD account when a threat is confirmed. You need to set up your BYD account first.
surveillance.deterrent_hint: Flashing the lights and sounding the horn go through BYD's servers, which pass the command on to the car's T-Box. You need to set up your BYD account below.
surveillance.deterrent_warning: No BYD account set up yet. Enter your login below to use the Warn-off.
surveillance.byd_cloud_hint: Link your BYD app account to send commands to the car (lock doors, flash lights, horn). Only scrambled key codes are kept — your real password is never stored.
surveillance.byd_region_desc: Has to be the region where your BYD account was created. Not sure? Try Europe (EU) first — most accounts outside China use it.
surveillance.byd_cloud_merge: Take car data from the BYD account
surveillance.byd_cloud_merge_desc: Battery, charging and temperature from your BYD account — can be more exact when parked
surveillance.storage_location_desc: Choose where the Guardian saves its clips
surveillance.post_event_buffer_desc: Seconds still filmed after the movement stops
surveillance.pre_event_buffer_desc: Seconds filmed before the movement started
surveillance.camera_fps_desc: Same value as for filming. Applies from the next time you park.
surveillance.recording_quality_desc: Picture quality for filming while parked, separate from the drive camera. Higher levels keep more detail but need more storage.
surveillance.camera_fps_desc_split: Frame rate for filming while parked, separate from the drive camera. A lower rate saves power and storage while parked.
surveillance.telegram_not_paired: Telegram isn't linked yet — the level switches do nothing until you link it.
surveillance.deterrent_hint_v2: Flashing the lights and sounding the horn go through your BYD account. Set it up first on the BYD account page (menu → System → BYD account).
surveillance.deterrent_warning_v2: Please set up your BYD account first.
surveillance.geocoding_enabled_name: Add place names to Guardian clips
surveillance.geocoding_enabled_desc: Turns the position at the start of a clip into a district or town name and saves it with the clip. Off normally, so the address of your home doesn't end up in shared messages.
surveillance.geocoding_online_desc: If the device can't name a place by itself, OpenStreetMap Nominatim is asked. Only the start position of the clip and your device language are sent.
surveillance.geocoding_custom_url_desc: Optional. Enter your own server so the public OSM service isn't used at all. The same address is used by the drive camera.
surveillance.geocoding_enabled_toast: Place names are added to Guardian clips
surveillance.geocoding_disabled_toast: Guardian clips get no place names
surveillance.geocoding_update_failed: Couldn't change the place names setting
surveillance.screen_deterrent_enable: Show a warning when something moves
surveillance.screen_deterrent_enable_desc: Wakes the screen of the car and shows a full-screen warning when movement is spotted. Works without a BYD account.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_duration_desc: How long the warning stays up after the movement stops. As long as something keeps moving, it stays.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_message_desc: Your own text instead of the standard notice (“Vehicle protected”, while recording “Camera recording”). Please only write what is true.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_content_help: Choose ONE: your own text on the standard red screen, OR your own picture, GIF or MP4 clip. If you set both, the upload wins.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_override_banner: A file is set, so your text is not used. Remove the file to use text instead.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_image: Your own picture, GIF or video
surveillance.screen_deterrent_image_desc: PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF up to 8 MB, or an MP4 clip up to 10 s, 1080p and 10 MB. A video repeats while the warning is shown; it plays without sound.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_remove_confirm: Delete the uploaded file? The Warn-off goes back to the standard red screen.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_preview_label_video: Video in use — repeats on screen
surveillance.screen_deterrent_hint: The screen only wakes up while the car is off. Once the car is switched on, the Warn-off stays quiet.
surveillance.screen_deterrent_too_large: Picture is too big (8 MB at most)
surveillance.screen_deterrent_video_too_large: Video is too big (10 MB at most)
surveillance.screen_deterrent_empty_file: That file has nothing in it
surveillance.screen_deterrent_bad_response: The server answered in an odd way
surveillance.screen_deterrent_remove_body: The Warn-off goes back to the standard red screen. You can't undo this.
surveillance.byd_clear_creds_body: Warn-off with lights and horn stops working until you set it up again.
surveillance.oem_record: Also film with the car's own drive camera
surveillance.oem_record_desc: Saves a matching dvr_*.mp4 from the front camera next to the all-round clip. The same quiet zones, schedule and camera filters apply as for the all-round Guardian.
surveillance.oem_record_enabled: The car's own drive camera now films with the Guardian
surveillance.oem_record_disabled: The car's own drive camera no longer films with the Guardian
surveillance.oem_id_unset_hint: First pick the number of the drive camera: System → Diagnostics → Camera test.
surveillance.telemetry_show_desc: Prints car data into the clips made while the car is off. Independent of the data shown on clips made while the car is on.
surveillance.telemetry_fields_desc: Choose what is printed into the Guardian clips.
surveillance.disabled_deferred: Guardian is off and won't start the next time you park
surveillance.enabled_deferred: Guardian starts the next time you switch the car off
surveillance.screen_deterrent_video_too_long: Video is too long (10 s at most). It repeats, so keep it short
surveillance.screen_deterrent_video_too_big: Video picture is too large (1920x1080 at most)
surveillance.keep_usb_power_capability_note: This mode can keep Android awake. But USB and SD card power while parked is only "best effort", because the car's own software controls the power line.

surveillance.screen_deterrent_save_failed: The screen warn-off was not stored

mqtt.err_name_required: Please give the link a name
mqtt.empty_p: No links yet. Add one to send your car's data.
mqtt.tailscale_hint: Using a private broker on your tailnet? Turn on the Tailscale proxy in the Remote access settings. Then it works without port forwarding. While it is on, public brokers can't be reached.
mqtt.wireguard_hint: Prefer a simple WireGuard link to your home network? Set it up on the WireGuard page.
mqtt.adaptive_desc: Sends less often while the car is parked
mqtt.retain_desc: The broker remembers the last message for new subscribers
mqtt.field_parked_interval_desc: How often a keep-alive goes out while the car is parked. Off = the longest gap applies. Higher = fewer messages, less data.
mqtt.field_charging_interval_desc: How often a keep-alive goes out while the car is charging. Off = the longest gap applies. This wins over the setting for parking.
mqtt.change_only_desc: Nothing is sent if no value changed (a keep-alive still goes out at the longest gap)
mqtt.ha_discovery_desc: Creates the devices in Home Assistant by itself. Each field is sent on its own and kept by the broker (no combined JSON).
mqtt.heartbeat_send_all_desc: Resends every value on each keep-alive, even if nothing changed. Brings everything up to date after a dropped connection.
mqtt.flush_on_state_change_desc: Resends every value when the car changes mode (engine on/off, charging starts/stops). That way HA always gets the new state, even if one update gets lost when the network switches. Costs very little, as it only happens on a change.
mqtt.allow_control_desc: Shows what can be controlled (climate, windows, seats, settings …) and carries out commands from Home Assistant. Works over the local SDK only, never through the BYD account. Off by default.

abrp.enable_desc: Sends live data from your car to A Better Route Planner
abrp.change_only_desc: Nothing is sent if no value changed. A keep-alive still goes out at the longest gap.
abrp.gate_on_app: Send only while ABRP is open
abrp.gate_on_app_desc: Sends data only while the ABRP app is open on this screen. Otherwise nothing is sent.
abrp.extern_text: Data goes to the ABRP service (Iternio). For routes and charging stops, use the Panoptes route planner instead; your data stays with us there.
abrp.apikey_missing: Missing. Panoptes does not include a key of its own; without one, nothing is sent to ABRP. You can get a key from Iternio (contact@iternio.com).

performance.data_usage_hint: Shows how much data Panoptes has used over the last 30 days (WiFi or mobile, app or background). Counting is off by default and takes hardly any power.
performance.data_usage_collecting: Counting now – the numbers will show up over the next few days.
performance.data_usage_unavailable: This device can't count data use per app.
performance.chart_hint: Touch or point to see the numbers
performance.gpu_sub_locked_high: Graphics chip stuck at full load
performance.gpu_sub_idle: Graphics chip resting, barely any power used
performance.gpu_hint_overloaded: ⚠️ The graphics chip is stuck at {pct}% and not easing off. The system may be overloaded or slowed down by heat.
performance.gpu_hint_healthy: ✓ That up and down is normal! The graphics chip jumps to {pct}% to draw the picture, then rests. This saves power.
performance.gpu_hint_efficient: {pct}% at {freq} MHz – speed is kept economical.
performance.gpu_hint_heavy: {pct}% at {freq} MHz – keep an eye on heat and battery use.
performance.soh_no_estimate: ⚠ No battery health value yet – waiting for data.
performance.soh_pinned_to: 📌 Locked to the {source} source. Switch to Auto for the blended value (EMA).
performance.soh_source_caption: Battery health source (used by route planner link, logbook, smart home link, range (estimated))
performance.cat_trips_desc: Trips, routes, weekly and monthly summaries, consumption figures
performance.cat_soc_history_desc: All battery readings, charging sessions and starter battery voltage logs
performance.cat_soh_desc: Detects the rated size again and restarts the estimate from the battery management system (BMS)
performance.cat_abrp_token_desc: Stops sending to ABRP until you pair again
performance.cat_byd_cloud_desc: User name, login key, VIN, region – you will need to sign in again
performance.cat_recordings_desc: Deletes every MP4 file in the clips folder
performance.cat_sentry_events_desc: Guardian clips and their JSON companion files
performance.cat_trip_telemetry_desc: Per-trip JSON data on the disk (database entries belong to the logbook above)
performance.soc_will_appear: The history will show once data has been collected
performance.soc_history_will_build: The history fills in over time

byd_cloud.recommend_title: Use a second access for the car
byd_cloud.recommend_sub: Best choice: your main BYD account stays separate. Tap to see the steps.
byd_cloud.recommend_step_1: Start the BYD app on your phone.
byd_cloud.recommend_step_4: Type in a second email address. It cannot be the one from your main account.
byd_cloud.recommend_step_5: Pick how long this access should last.
byd_cloud.recommend_step_6: Sign out of the BYD app. Then register with the second email: enter the code you receive and set a password.
byd_cloud.recommend_step_7: In the BYD app, tap Lock or Unlock. It asks you to create a control PIN.
byd_cloud.recommend_step_8: Now type the second email, the password and the control PIN into Panoptes.

telegram.connect_failed: No link. Check the token and your internet.
telegram.confirm_clear: Delete the bot token, the linked account and your choices?
telegram.pair_intro: Create a PIN that works once. Then, in the Telegram app on your phone, send "/pair <PIN>" to the bot. The PIN is valid for 10 minutes.
telegram.pair_empty: First enter the bot token on the Bot tab. Then return here to link your Telegram account.
telegram.pin_expired: PIN is no longer valid. Create a new one.
telegram.confirm_unpair: Send no more alerts to this Telegram account?
telegram.video_uploads_desc: Sends short clips with critical alerts. This uses more data, so turn it off if your connection is slow.
telegram.tiers_pointer: Which levels get through (Notice / Alert / Critical) is set under Alerts → Telegram.
telegram.load_failed: Telegram state could not be fetched
telegram.critical_alerts_desc: Things that need you right away: car faults, someone tampering, charging problems. Better leave this on.
telegram.connectivity_updates_desc: Tells you when the service starts, stops or restarts. Handy for finding problems, otherwise a bit chatty.
telegram.motion_text_desc: Sends a message when Guardian sees movement, with a photo if there is one. Video clips have their own switch below.
telegram.auto_start_acc_off: Start itself when the car is off
telegram.auto_start_acc_off_desc: Starts the Telegram service when the car is switched off (ACC OFF), so commands work while it is parked. It stops once the car is started.
telegram.daemon_start_pointer: Starting and stopping by hand is done on the Services page in the app on the car.
telegram.delivery_pointer: Which events reach the chat is set under Alerts → Telegram.
telegram.tyre_alerts_desc: Sends a Telegram message if a tyre's pressure leaves your chosen range, or the tyre sensor reports a leak. Uses the limits from Tyre pressure limits.
telegram.parking_messages_desc: Sends "Parked" (place, how fresh the GPS is, Guardian state, a photo from all four cameras) and "Back at car" (how long you were away, events, cars that came or left). Needs the Parking log in the Guardian settings.
telegram.always_on_note: The service is switched on in the app on the car, so it runs no matter what this switch says, even when parked. Switch it off there to stop it.

dashboard.subtitle: How your car is, where it is, and the main buttons.

oem_dashcam.title: Car's own dashcam
oem_dashcam.id_unset_desc: Go to Diagnostics → Camera Probe and choose which AVMCamera number is the front dashcam. On Auto, it is the surround camera's number flipped between 0 and 1. On Seal and Han the surround camera is 1, so the car's own dashcam is 0.
oem_dashcam.enable: Record with the car's own dashcam
oem_dashcam.enable_hint: Saves the front camera as dvr_*.mp4. Quality, codec and frame rate come from the Quality tab.
oem_dashcam.telemetry_overlay: Print driving data into the video
oem_dashcam.telemetry_overlay_desc: Burns speed, GPS and time into dvr_*.mp4. Works separately from the surround camera's setting.
oem_dashcam.telemetry_fields_desc: Pick what is shown on the video of the car's own dashcam.
oem_dashcam.acc_off_hint: Off: recording ends when the car is switched off. 24/7: keeps recording while parked. This uses a little power from the 12 V battery.
oem_dashcam.status_hint: Your settings are kept already. Recording begins once the background service is ready.
oem_dashcam.status_hint_off: Choose Always or Smart above to switch on recording with the car's front camera.
oem_dashcam.status_hint_continuous_recording: Records without a break. New dvr_*.mp4 files start every few minutes. The surround camera still writes its own cam_*.mp4 files at the same time.
oem_dashcam.status_hint_smart_recording: Follows the surround camera. dvr_*.mp4 starts when it starts (Always, Drive mode or when someone gets close) and ends when it ends.
oem_dashcam.status_hint_continuous_surveillance: Records the whole time the car is parked, movement or not. Needs the most space, but suits risky spots.
oem_dashcam.status_hint_smart_surveillance: Follows the Guardian. dvr_*.mp4 starts once movement and AI agree it is a person or car, next to the event_*.mp4 of the surround camera. The same quiet zones and schedule apply.
oem_dashcam.recording_mode_desc: Decides when the front camera saves dvr_*.mp4 next to the cam_*.mp4 clips of the surround camera.
oem_dashcam.surveillance_mode_desc: Decides when the front camera saves dvr_*.mp4 as part of the Guardian (movement near the parked car).
oem_dashcam.mode_off_desc_recording: The car's front camera does not record. The surround camera keeps writing cam_*.mp4 as usual.
oem_dashcam.mode_continuous_desc_recording: Writes dvr_*.mp4 the whole time Panoptes runs, whatever the surround camera does.
oem_dashcam.mode_smart_desc_recording: Does what the surround camera does: when it records (Drive mode, Always, or someone close), dvr_*.mp4 records too. When it stops, so does this one.
oem_dashcam.mode_off_desc_surveillance: The car's front camera does not record for the Guardian. The surround camera keeps writing event_*.mp4 as usual.
oem_dashcam.mode_continuous_desc_surveillance: Writes dvr_*.mp4 for as long as the car is parked, movement or not. This fills your storage fastest.
oem_dashcam.mode_smart_desc_surveillance: Follows the surround camera: once movement is seen and AI agrees it is a person or car, dvr_*.mp4 is saved next to event_*.mp4. Quiet zones, schedule and per-camera filters apply as for the Guardian.
oem_dashcam.recording_mode_set_smart: Car's dashcam while driving: automatic (follows surround camera)
oem_dashcam.surveillance_mode_set_smart: Car's dashcam while parked: automatic (follows surround camera)
oem_dashcam.native_dvr_explainer: BYD's own dashcam app saves to /sdcard/DCIM/BYDCam and grabs AVMCamera every time the car is switched on (ACC ON). Turn it off so Panoptes can use the camera alone.
oem_dashcam.native_dvr_disable_toast: Built-in DVR is off. Panoptes has the camera to itself.
oem_dashcam.start_timeout: Start took too long. Look at the service logs.

keymap.enable_desc: Main switch. When it is off, every button works as it did from the factory. Nothing is intercepted.
keymap.allow_advanced_desc: Allows buttons that run a raw shell command. Keep this off unless you know exactly what you send.
keymap.double_tap_window_desc: How long the car waits for a second tap before it counts as a single tap. If double-taps often trigger the single action, make it longer. If a single tap feels slow, make it shorter.
keymap.a11y_needed: To catch the car’s buttons, Panoptes needs its accessibility service switched on. Your settings are saved, but they only work once it is on.
keymap.a11y_pending: The service is on and starting. The buttons work in a few seconds. You don’t need to do anything.
keymap.a11y_hint: Look for Panoptes in the list and switch it on.
keymap.capture_hint: Tap “Detect a button”, then press the wheel or dash button you want to change. The car’s own software handles some buttons, so Panoptes never sees them. If nothing shows up, that button can’t be changed.
keymap.capture_press: Press a button in the car now…
keymap.manual_keycode_help: Android key code, e.g. 87 = next song, 88 = previous song.
keymap.block_native_single_desc: Stops the button’s usual function from firing before your press-twice action. Pressing once still works, only a little later.
keymap.native_side_effect_warn: The car runs this button’s built-in function (mute / Bluetooth) by itself. It may still happen along with your action, and an app can’t fully stop it. Tip: use “Press twice” with “Block the single tap”. That works best.
keymap.split_screen_desc: Starts the app on one half of the screen instead of full screen.
keymap.shell_warn: Runs on every press with the service’s full rights. A bad command can upset the car’s infotainment. “Expert actions” must be on.
keymap.need_keycode: Detect a button or type a key code first.
keymap.empty_hint: Press a button in the car to detect it, then pick what it should do.
keymap.clip_window_hint: A clip can be up to 60 seconds long.
keymap.clip_window_invalid: Pick a length in whole seconds, from 1 to 60.
keymap.clip_sequence_unsupported: Saving the last moments needs its own button. You can’t put it into a chain of steps.
keymap.clip_restart_required: Saved. To get the full length, do a full restart of the camera service under Services. The drive camera was not interrupted.
keymap.editing: You are changing this assignment. Save to keep it.
keymap.no_audio: No sounds yet. Upload some under Rules.
keymap.no_automations: No rules yet. Create one under Rules.
keymap.sequence_hint: Add one action, or chain several with “Add a step” so one button runs them all.
keymap.act_cast_app_cluster: Show an app on the driver display
keymap.qc_desc: Saves the action above as a shortcut on Home, so no physical button is needed.
keymap.act_camview_side_rear_left_cluster: Driver display cameras: rear + left side
keymap.act_camview_side_rear_right_cluster: Driver display cameras: rear + right side
keymap.battery_hold_at_current: Keep the battery as it is
keymap.need_action_group: Pick an action group to start.
keymap.no_action_groups: No action groups yet. Create one under Rules.
keymap.qc_confirm_delete: Remove this shortcut? The action itself stays.
keymap.qc_need_action: Pick what the shortcut should do.

network.warn_title: The car will drop its WiFi
network.warn_body: The car has only one WiFi chip. It can’t run a hotspot and stay on WiFi at the same time. While the hotspot is on, the car leaves WiFi and uses its built-in SIM, for itself and for every connected device. WiFi returns when you switch the hotspot off.
network.enable_desc: Makes the car a WiFi network that shares the internet from its built-in SIM.
network.credentials_note: The car decides the hotspot name and password, so you can’t change them here. Tap one to copy it.
network.limit_desc: When the hotspot has used this much data, it switches off and you get an alert. Leave it empty for no cap. It limits the total amount, not the speed.
network.keepalive_desc: If the hotspot drops by itself, it starts again.
network.autostart_desc: Switches the hotspot on once each time the car powers up.
network.proxy_system: Send the car’s own traffic through the proxy
network.proxy_system_desc: Sets the proxy for the whole car, so its apps use the encrypted tunnel. The proxy service must be running.
network.proxy_clients_desc: Makes the proxy available on the hotspot. Each device must enter the proxy in its own WiFi settings. Joining alone doesn’t send its traffic through.
network.proxy_clients_desc_fmt: Joining the hotspot isn’t enough. The car can’t send devices online by itself, so each device must use the car’s proxy. After joining on the device: 1) open its WiFi settings and edit this network, 2) set Proxy to Manual, 3) enter host name {gw} and port {port}, 4) save, then browse. The device may still say “no internet” and show its own mobile-data icon even when this works, because that check ignores proxies.
network.limit_invalid: Type a whole number of megabytes.
network.client_tunnel_desc_fmt: Sends the devices’ traffic through the encrypted tunnel before it leaves the car’s SIM. On the devices, use port {tp} instead of {rp}. It is slower because of the extra stop. When you switch this off, that port closes at once.

genai.empty_desc: You write, Panoptes answers. Car data is only shared when you pick a car-based question or ask for it yourself.
genai.enable_desc: The main switch. When it is off, running requests stop and the connection to the AI service is closed.
genai.base_url_hint: Use HTTPS if you can. Plain HTTP is fine for a trusted service in your own network.
genai.realtime_hint: Only for services that can talk live themselves. Panoptes never swaps in a separate speech-to-text step.
genai.privacy_title: Your data and how it runs
genai.checking_runtime: Checking the AI part inside your car.
genai.show_on_dashboard: Show the newest tip on Home
genai.show_on_dashboard_desc: The newest saved tip shows on the car's home screen and on the web Home page. Only while AI is turned on.
genai.notify_when_ready: Alert me when it is done
genai.notify_when_ready_desc: If this is off, regular summaries are just saved in your car. No alert is sent.
genai.schedule_note: Home only shows text that already exists. Showing it never contacts the AI service. Daily and weekly use the clock of the rules. Want a tip after a drive, after charging, on a road watch spot or at another moment? Add the action “Generate AI insight” in Rules.
genai.model_hint: Pick one from the list or type any model name your service knows.
genai.key_keep: Leave empty to keep your saved key.
genai.key_saved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it
genai.key_encrypted: Your key is locked away in the car. The browser never gets it back.
genai.custom_realtime_model: Your own live voice model name
genai.privacy_1: Your key is stored locked and tied to this car, the same way as the BYD account login. This page never gets it back.
genai.privacy_2: The chat lives only in this page's memory. It is gone when you close or reload the page.
genai.privacy_3: Car data goes out only when you pick a car-based question. It counts as plain facts and is never treated as an order for the AI.
genai.privacy_4: When you start voice, the car opens a live voice link to the service. It closes when you stop, when you leave this page, or after a quiet spell.
genai.privacy_5: Main switch off: running requests stop and every connection to the service is closed.
genai.privacy_6: Every request checks the Panoptes proxy route again. If a Tailscale proxy should be used but is missing, the request stops. It does not go out directly.
genai.voice_note: The microphone only shows for services that can talk live themselves. Panoptes adds no separate speech-to-text step.
genai.voice_unavailable: This service cannot do live voice
genai.state_off_desc: The main switch is off. No connection to a service and no AI work in the background.
genai.state_setup_desc: Enter a chat model and a key, then save.
genai.transport_idle: Resting · no link to the service
genai.start_voice_native: Start live voice with the service
genai.connecting_realtime: Linking up with the live voice service…
genai.voice_tap_hint: Tap the microphone to talk live. Typing stays the standard.
genai.suggested_models: Ideas: {list}. Your own model names work too.
genai.enter_model_id: Type the model name your service gives you.
genai.optional_bearer: Bearer key, only if needed. A saved key from one service is never used for another.
genai.enter_new_key: Please enter a new key for {provider}.
genai.confirm_clear: Turn AI off and delete the saved key from this car?
genai.cleared_toast: AI is off and the key is deleted
genai.choose_time: Pick a proper time of day
genai.no_community: No matching rules from other drivers. Try describing it more closely.
genai.confirm_hint: Nothing runs until you say yes. The usual safety checks of the car and the rules still apply.
genai.share_once: Share just for this spoken answer
genai.no_vehicle_shared: No car data left the car.
genai.invalid_daemon: The car service sent an answer that makes no sense.
genai.request_timeout: The car took too long to answer.
genai.request_start_failed: The request to the car could not be started.
genai.parked_on_only_desc: This car runs in on-only mode, so the service stops once the car is switched off.
genai.key_protected: A key is saved and locked. Leave empty to keep it.
genai.enter_new_key_full: Enter a new key for {provider}. A key saved for one service is never used for another.
genai.tap_to_stop: tap the microphone again to stop
genai.community_found: {count} matching rules from other drivers. Look through them below or take one over.
genai.community_found_one: One matching rule from another driver. Look at it below or take it over.

genai.confirm_save_draft: Save this as a draft that starts by hand only? It will never run on its own.
genai.confirm_import: Take over "{name}" and keep it off until you have checked it?

genai.shared_once_ok: Fresh data without private details was shared one time.
genai.share_until_approve: Nothing leaves the car until you agree. Logs are blacked out first. Exact locations, logins and file paths stay out.
genai.no_realtime_audio: This browser cannot handle live audio
genai.mode_diagnostic_logs: Log extracts with details blacked out

genai.voice_too_slow: Your connection is too slow for live voice

system.services_note: Turning on takes about 30 seconds. Turning off works at once.
system.core_note: Camera, Guardian and Guardian on park always run. The camera service also carries this web page.
system.login_waiting: Tailscale is waiting for you to sign in:
system.pair_lead: So that e.g. EV Cockpit can show and change Panoptes settings. Remote access, password and ports stay locked for paired devices.

trigger.title: When should the Guardian record?
trigger.intro: It's your choice. AI detection records video and photos as soon as someone comes close to the car, so you also see who was just looking. But it also films people who are only walking past.

a.label: Only on impact
a.desc: Records only if someone bumps or damages the car. Fine everywhere.

b.label: AI detection everywhere
b.desc: Also records when someone comes close, wherever you park. On streets and in public car parks this can lead to a fine, because strangers are filmed. Not available in Switzerland.
b.note: Outside your private property, you are responsible for making sure recording is allowed.

c.label: AI detection only at my private places
c.desc: Records when someone comes close only at places you choose, e.g. your garage or driveway. Elsewhere only on impact. On your own property this is usually allowed, as long as the camera doesn't also film the street or your neighbour's property.
c.placesHint: Only places you own or are allowed to use. Make sure the Guardian doesn't film the street.
c.noPlaces: No private place set yet. Until then the Guardian only records on impact.

trigger.footer: You're responsible for your clips. You can change this at any time.

rechtshinweis.text: Panoptes can show known speed cameras on the map (data from OpenStreetMap). Only turn the display on where this is allowed. You are responsible for that yourself. The same applies to sounds and voice announcements: an audible warning is forbidden there too. Panoptes only gives a warning while driving in Austria. Not legal advice, as of 10/2026. The law may change; check the rules of your country.

wallbox.find_hint: Searches for about 5 seconds in the Wi-Fi the car is connected to (read only). This does not work on the road – use Home Assistant or the manufacturer account instead.
wallbox.find_none: No wallbox found in the Wi-Fi. Is the car connected to your home Wi-Fi? Otherwise: Home Assistant or manufacturer account.
wallbox.find_tuya_schluessel: This wallbox can be controlled via Home Assistant. How: set up the official Tuya integration in Home Assistant (sign-in via QR code with the Smart Life app), then choose “Home Assistant” above and “Sign in with Home Assistant”.
wallbox.find_nur_ueber_ha: Fronius Wattpilot only works via Home Assistant.
wallbox.ha_logged_in: Signed in with Home Assistant – no token needed.
wallbox.ha_login_hint: Enter the address of your Home Assistant above (found in the Wi-Fi), then sign in with your normal HA account. A long-lived token is no longer needed.
wallbox.err_anmeldung_abgelaufen: Home Assistant sign-in expired – please sign in again.
wallbox.err_zu_viele_anmeldungen: Too many open sign-ins – please try again in 10 minutes.
wallbox.hint_bruecke_gesperrt: The wallbox bridge does not allow control right now – display only. Only the bridge operator can enable it.
wallbox.err_bruecke_gesperrt: The wallbox bridge has blocked control.
wallbox.err_bruecke_keine_quittung: The wallbox bridge did not answer – command not confirmed.
wallbox.err_bruecke_abgelehnt: The wallbox bridge rejected the command.
wallbox.find_bruecke_gesperrt: Found. Control is currently blocked at the bridge – Panoptes will only display.
wallbox.found_auto: Wallbox found – tap to use it.

orte.lead: One list for all places where Panoptes should behave differently: private (no recording), quiet zone (guardian off), home (monthly report) and charging price. Places never leave the car.
orte.karte_hint: Tap the map to set the centre of the selected place.
orte.name: Name
orte.e_zuhause_hint: Counts as “charged at home” in the monthly report.
orte.t_dc: DC per kWh (empty = same as AC)
orte.favorit_hint: Also a navigation favourite (editable here with a later update).
orte.nicht_verfuegbar: Places come with a Panoptes update.
orte.mitte_fehlt: Tap the map to set the centre.
orte.preis_fehlt: Please enter an AC price or choose “free”.
orte.loeschen_frage: Delete “{name}”? Quiet zone, private area and charging price of this place will be removed.
orte.kein_gps: No location from the car – please set it on the map.
orte.verweis: Quiet zones, private areas and charging places are now together under
orte.e_favorit_hint2: Shown in navigation as a quick destination.

notz.text: Emergency access is a second, independent way into the car for remote maintenance – in case the normal remote access ever stops working. It runs over your own Tailscale network (tailnet): only devices in your tailnet can reach it, and even then only for maintenance (adb), not the Panoptes interface. You can switch it off here at any time; the way is then closed immediately.
notz.nur_im_auto: Can only be set in the car or when logged in, not from a paired device.
notz.name: Device name
notz.key_hint: To set it up you need an auth key from your Tailscale admin (Settings → Keys, starts with “tskey-”). It is handed to the emergency access once and never stored or shown.
notz.an_frage: Switch on emergency access? Devices in your tailnet can then reach the car for maintenance.

eingr.text: Panoptes changes some Android settings only as long as needed. Here you see the current state. Before uninstalling you can reset everything to its original value.
eingr.frage: Reset system settings? “Screen stays on while charging” returns to its original value and power saving is switched back on. Panoptes keeps running.
